description: I’m a student interested in software development, data engineering, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies. I’m building a team for NASA Space Apps Challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. I’m looking for motivated teammates eager to learn, collaborate, and build. Especially seeking UX/UI designers, coders, frontend/backend developers, data engineers, GIS, AI/ML, and cybersecurity enthusiasts.
summary:
Two satellite fire products disagree about the same landscape: MODIS and VIIRS detect different thermal anomalies at different times and with different pixel sizes, and a day with no overpass can be mistaken for a day with no fire. Harmonova processes real NASA FIRMS archive detections, maps them onto a common 0.05° grid and local solar day, and combines reported activity into a cell-day union while preserving every sensor's individual contribution.

Missing or incomplete observation days remain gaps, never zeros. The documented Aqua outage of August–September 2020 is represented as a gap for Aqua while other sensors continue reporting. The result is a reproducible processing pipeline and offline-capable browser viewer built around 120,720 real satellite detections.
details:
Project Overview

Harmonova is a reproducible data-processing platform that addresses the challenges of comparing MODIS and VIIRS satellite active-fire observations. These sensors differ in spatial resolution, observation timing, detection characteristics, and confidence classifications. Simply combining their raw detections can cause double-counting, while missing observations can incorrectly appear as zero fire activity.

How It Works

The project processes NASA FIRMS standard-processing archive data from MODIS Collection 6.1 (Aqua and Terra) and VIIRS 375 m Suomi-NPP Collection 2.

Its processing pipeline performs five main stages:

  1. Data acquisition and provenance tracking using source manifests, SHA-256 checksums, file sizes, and row counts.
  2. Strict ingestion, validation, and normalization of satellite detection records.
  3. Declared filtering profiles with duplicate detection, confidence filtering, and rejection auditing.
  4. Spatial harmonization using a common 0.05-degree grid and local solar-day assignment.
  5. Generation of sensor-specific activity, cell-day unions, quality indicators, and schema-validated JSON exports.

The browser-based viewer provides five sections: Calendar, Map, Sensors, Quality, and Methods. It allows users to inspect individual sensor observations, compare sensor contributions, identify missing-data periods, and understand the limitations of the results.

Demonstration Results

The demonstration covers August 1 to October 31, 2020, within an area bounded by 36.0–40.5°N and 122.0–118.0°W.

The pipeline processed 120,720 real NASA FIRMS detection records with zero rejected rows. After the declared filtering profile, 116,395 detections remained eligible. The resulting outputs include 10,596 sensor-specific cell-days and 5,998 union active cell-days across 91 days.

A key feature is its treatment of missing observations: incomplete ingestion and documented satellite outages remain distinguishable from confirmed zero activity. This is demonstrated through the historical Aqua outage and other incomplete observation periods.

Technology and Tools

Python 3.12, pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, PyYAML, requests, jsonschema, pytest, Docker Compose, NGINX, HTML, CSS, JavaScript ES modules, Leaflet, Apache ECharts, and OpenStreetMap map tiles.

Limitations

Satellite detections represent thermal anomalies, not confirmed incident counts, fire perimeters, burned area, or emissions. Observation opportunity and cloud coverage remain unassessed. Sensor-native confidence and fire radiative power values are not harmonized. The optional calibration bridge is disabled, and the selected configuration remains provisional.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

AI assistance was used throughout project planning, implementation and review. GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, accessed through coding-agent workflows, assisted with source-code generation, debugging, tests and software implementation. ChatGPT assisted with architectural planning, execution-prompt preparation, technical review, scientific QA guidance, documentation and submission drafting. The project owner directed the work and reviewed implementation and outputs.

All reported satellite observations originate from actual NASA FIRMS source files; analytical values were generated by the project's deterministic processing pipeline, not invented by an AI model. No AI-generated imagery was used in the submitted demonstration.

The AI tools are not authors of the project and do not take responsibility for its content; the team does. Every screenshot in the project documentation is a capture of the running application with real data.

The project is not endorsed by NASA.
